newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Minister could outlaw new Colombian truck strike.
newsitem.headline: Minister could outlaw new Colombian truck strike.

text.p: Transport Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez threatened Monday to outlaw a strike by Colombian truck drivers scheduled for April 20.

At a meeting Saturday, the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), which represents about 80 percent of the nation's truckers, voted to strike in protest at transport companies' failure to fulfill the terms of a deal signed at the end of a crippling 11-day stoppage in October.
In comments to local media, Lopez said he would declare a fresh strike illegal on grounds that transport was an "essential public service".
The government adopted the same tactic in October, but truckers resisted the return-to-work order arguing that as private sector contractors they were not obliged to work if they chose not to.

The accord hammered out to end the truckers' October strike was backed by the government and included provisions for an increase in freight rates, downtime payments to truckers while they waited to on- and off-load cargoes and a revision of vehicle licensing fees and highway tolls.
But ACC national directorate member Mario Quiroga said none of the terms of that agreement have been fulfilled and said truckers were still being forced to operate at a loss.
The strike in October paralyzed virtually all road freight, including at least 305,000 60-kg bags of key coffee exports.
News of another stoppage has set alarm bells ringing among private coffee exporters, who warn it could deal a severe blow to April export schedules.
